title: Harness Continual Learning: Continual Adaptation Beyond Model Parameters

visual_explainer.blocker: No paper-specific visual is published until a grounded state-commit figure passes visual-policy review; the verified deep note carries the evidence meanwhile.

analysis.tldr: Harness Continual Learning treats prompts, experience memory, capability maps, and routing rules as jointly versioned adaptive state around a frozen model, then separates candidate generation from commitment through current-task, historical-retention, and validity checks.
analysis.problem: An agent can forget earlier behavior even when model weights are frozen because updates to prompts, memories, tools, skills, or routing change what later executions see and do. Continual-learning controls therefore have to cover the harness state itself.
analysis.core_idea: Evolve an execution-facing Task Interface, Experience Memory, Capability Map, and Adaptive Router as one candidate harness, evaluate current improvement and historical anchors, and commit only candidates that satisfy validity and a configurable retention bound.

memory_design.write: Post-execution feedback produces raw and abstract experiences plus candidate changes to the interface, capability map, and router.
memory_design.organize: Version the four harness components jointly so a candidate state and its provenance can be evaluated before commitment.
memory_design.read: The task interface, experience memory, capability map, and adaptive router jointly condition action selection by the frozen foundation model.
memory_design.update_forget: A continual evaluator tests current utility, historical retention, and validity before atomic commit; explicit retention bounds expose harness-level forgetting.

compared_to: Static Harness, RAG, MemP, and MemRL under a unified execution stack
Full HCL versus removal of the Experience Memory update
Controlled historical-loss tolerance sweeps from strict retention to unrestricted commitment
analysis.evidence: On ALFWorld, RAG reaches 55.56 final average, Stability-HCL 61.74, and Plasticity-HCL 62.98, but the plastic setting incurs 10.94 forgetting. In the retention sweep, unrestricted commitment ends at 60.13 versus 63.46 at b=1. Removing memory update yields 62.28/0.83 forgetting versus 63.41/0.45 for Full HCL, a narrow memory-stage witness inside a broader interacting package.
analysis.why_it_matters: The persistent state of an agent extends beyond a memory store. Treating harness changes as versioned, testable commits makes stability-plasticity and rollback boundaries explicit without pretending that frozen weights imply frozen behavior.
limitations: The system jointly changes four harness components; headline gains belong to the evolving package, not the memory component alone.
The memory ablation remains inside a co-adaptive system and may contain interaction effects.
Historical anchors and validity checks are benchmark-specific and may not cover latent deployment regressions.
The paper does not report a complete construction, evaluation, storage, and serving lifecycle cost or public code.
